Why do hearing aids average $3,432 a pair?
That's the private-pay prescription average in HearingTracker's 2025 buyer survey, often bundled with the hearing test, fitting and follow-ups.
Five makers control about 90% of the global market and 84% in the US (2025 estimate).
Original Medicare doesn't cover hearing aids (some Medicare Advantage plans offer benefits). Since Oct 17, 2022, adults 18+ with perceived mild-to-moderate loss can buy OTC pairs, which averaged $502 in the same survey.
Our math: $3,432 - $502 = $2,930.
Sources: HearingTracker (2025 survey), American Economic Liberties Project via The Capitol Forum, Medicare.gov, FDA.
News and education, not financial advice.
